findings.title: Explicit null SHA256 disables expected-byte verification
findings.observed: Compiler hash, library binary hash, configure log hash and install log hash set to null each admit altered bytes and return BYTE_CHAIN_VERIFIED.
findings.impact: A record missing mandatory identities is accepted. This is separate from the correctly disclosed inability to independently witness a forged complete build record.
findings.minimum_fix: Require each compiler/binary/log expected SHA256 to be a 64-hex string before checking bytes. Distinguish omitted expected hash for pure identity collection from explicitly null expected hash in verification. Add missing/null/malformed identity regressions.

supported_observations: Fixed archive SHA256 and exact length gates are present for the three pinned releases.
Canonical resolution rejects backend symlink escape from the sidecar prefix.
ldd parser binds each required soname family to the resolved expected backend path, rejects missing/duplicate/backend-path substitutions and returns check-time byte hashes.
The verification block explicitly withholds independently witnessed execution, historical ABI admission and scientific promotion.
The linkage function returns current hashes and assumes filesystem stability; cross-stage comparison remains a caller integration duty and the runner is outside this review.
